source.title: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning
source.authors: Dan Braun; Jordan K. Taylor; Nicholas Goldowsky-Dill; Lee Sharkey

record.tranche_reason: The study compares SAE training objectives and measures activation reconstruction and shrinkage. Its results bear on whether end-to-end training reduces reconstruction error, but it does not test the broader claim that most dark matter is a training artifact.
record.gate_note: The study does not test linear predictability, error norms across SAE sizes or token overlap across sizes, random errors matched in size, or a decomposition into two kinds of dark matter. Its cross-entropy comparisons measure performance when SAE outputs replace activations, but do not compare those effects with matched random errors or test whether downstream analyses retain behavior by keeping an error term. Figure-only reconstruction comparisons are included where the text explicitly describes their direction. Appendix G.3 also tests one poorly reconstructed PCA direction's functional importance; this is recorded as a related finding not covered by a version.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs with end-to-end objectives instead of local MSE on GPT2-small and reports their activation reconstruction error. This bears directly on V6's prediction that end-to-end training shrinks dark matter. The study predates and is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that e2e SAEs are a Pareto improvement: more performance explained with fewer active and total features, and no loss of interpretability. They accept worse activation reconstruction, and e2e+ds keeps downstream pathways close to the original model. They attribute part of the reconstruction gap to feature suppression and to functionally irrelevant directions. They argue that local SAEs capture dataset structure not useful for explaining the network.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces end-to-end SAE training with output-distribution KL loss, and an end-to-end-plus-downstream variant; it compares these with local SAE training. It does not reproduce the dark-matter analysis or its measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE training objective and type; layer; token position. The authors also report that normalization changes explained-variance comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: A direction that e2e+ds SAEs reconstruct poorly at nonzero positions (r=0.262) is nearly functionally irrelevant: resample-ablating it gives KL 0.01, the smallest among the first 30 PCA directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some SAE reconstruction error lies in functionally irrelevant directions, so activation-space error overstates functional loss.

record.problems: The reconstruction comparisons do not test linear predictability, token-by-token error overlap across SAE sizes, or comparisons with matched random errors. Several reconstruction values are only shown in figures without exact numbers. The principal comparisons use GPT2-small, with additional qualitative generalization to TinyStories-1M; the authors say more model sizes and architectures remain future work. V6's broad claim that most dark matter is a training artifact is not established by these results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No linear prediction of the SAE error from input activations.
No per-token error-norm prediction across SAE sizes and no same-context failure analysis. The dictionary-size sweep (Appendix E) reports only CE loss, L0 and alive-element counts.
No comparison with random errors of matched norm.
No decomposition into linear and nonlinear error parts and no test of their learnability.
No circuit or steering analysis with or without the error term.

Not tested: other architectures (gated, TopK), alternative sparsity penalties, and whether the residual error reflects model representation structure. Only local, e2e and e2e+ds residual-stream SAEs on GPT2-small are tested, with partial TinyStories-1M runs.

missing.what: Downstream-layer reconstruction MSE by SAE type. e2e is much higher than local at all later layers; e2e+ds is close to local at later layers but worse at the SAE layer.
Explained variance of reconstructed activations with and without layer-norm normalization. Normalization greatly improves e2e SAEs.
CE loss increase at fixed L0: e2e and e2e+ds are under 45% of local. Tables 2 and 3 give per-layer CE loss increases.
Increasing local SAE dictionary size (60x to 100x) or training samples (400k to 800k) does not noticeably improve the CE/L0 Pareto frontier.

record.verdict_notes: V6 is ambiguous here. End-to-end training increases activation-space error, which challenges V6, but shrinks the output-space functional gap. The reader's limits_scope label for e2e+ds was really an untested-parts statement, so it was replaced. The e2e+ds cosine rows show worse reconstruction too, so they join the challenges group. Norm-ratio rows are suggestive only, because the ratio gives a lower bound on error, not the error itself.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of input activations.
Whether error norms are predictable across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
The study does not compare SAE reconstruction errors with random errors of the same size.
The study does not decompose error into the proposed linear and nonlinear parts or test their learnability.
The study does not test circuits or steering with and without the SAE error term.

It tests local versus end-to-end and end-to-end-plus-downstream training in the reported settings, but not whether most dark matter is caused by training choices, other architectures, or end-to-end training that improves reconstruction.

relationships.condition: GPT2-small residual stream, layers 2/6/10, SAEs matched on CE loss increase: e2e and e2e+ds versus local SAEs
relationships.reason: End-to-end training enlarges activation reconstruction error at the SAE layer: worse cosine similarity (r19-r24, Fig. 11) and heavy norm suppression (r7-r13, r17, r18). The text says e2e SAEs are 'much worse at reconstructing the exact activation'.
relationships.display_finding: At matched cross-entropy loss increases, end-to-end and e2e+ds SAEs had worse activation cosine similarity and strong norm suppression compared with local SAEs.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: GPT2-small residual stream, layers 2/6/10, SAEs matched on CE loss increase: e2e and e2e+ds versus local SAEs
source_check.reason: Appendix B explicitly reports worse activation reconstruction, and B.2 reports worse directional reconstruction for both end-to-end variants. These support the verdict independently of the norm-ratio rows.

relationships.condition: Error measured in output space (CE loss increase) rather than activation space, or after layer-norm normalization
relationships.reason: Based on the text, as no row records these results. At equal L0, e2e SAEs cut CE loss increase to under 45% of local SAEs (Sec 3.1). Normalizing activations greatly improves e2e explained variance (App. B.3), so part of the e2e error is training-induced shrinkage. Whether training shrinks 'dark matter' therefore depends on how the error is measured.
relationships.display_finding: At equal L0, end-to-end SAEs reduced the cross-entropy loss increase to under 45% of local SAEs; activation normalization greatly improved their explained variance.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Error measured in output space (CE loss increase) rather than activation space, or after layer-norm normalization
source_check.reason: Lower output CE measures a different construct from activation dark matter. Evaluation-time normalization diagnoses a scale contribution but does not demonstrate that end-to-end training reduces activation error relative to local training; Appendix B.3 says the overall comparison remains similar. These are useful qualifications, but do not establish a separate V6 condition where its predicted reduction holds partially.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

tranche.reason: The study's controlled training-objective comparisons contradict the end-to-end activation-error reduction component of V6 and require distinguishing activation fidelity from output fidelity.

source_check.notes: The challenge concerns activation reconstruction at similar CE loss increase, with local SAEs using higher L0. The under-45% CE result instead compares equal L0; neither result establishes what proportion of dark matter is a training artifact.
